findings.title: Usage of `tx.origin` for authentication
findings.description: `tx.origin` returns the original sender of the transaction, not the immediate caller. Using it for authentication is vulnerable to phishing attacks where a malicious contract tricks a user into calling it, then forwards the call to the victim contract.
findings.recommendation: Replace `tx.origin` with `msg.sender` for authentication. `tx.origin` is only safe for checking that a call was initiated by an EOA (not a contract), but even that has edge cases.

findings.description: The expression `calcBase * _ethSlashAmount / rocketNetworkPrices.getRPLPrice` computes the multiplication first. If `calcBase * _ethSlashAmount` exceeds uint256 max, the transaction reverts even though the final result (after division) would fit. This is a "phantom overflow" issue.
findings.recommendation: Use `Math.mulDiv(calcBase, _ethSlashAmount, rocketNetworkPrices.getRPLPrice)` which handles the intermediate overflow safely using 512-bit math.

findings.title: Read-only reentrancy risk: `getOutstandingEth` may return stale data
findings.description: View function `getOutstandingEth` reads balance/share state that is also modified by `_claimAndStake` (which has external calls). If `_claimAndStake` makes an external call before updating state, a callback could invoke `getOutstandingEth` and get stale values. This is exploitable if other protocols rely on this view function.
findings.recommendation: Ensure state is updated before external calls in `_claimAndStake`. If this view function is used by external protocols for pricing, consider adding reentrancy protection.

findings.title: Unsigned to signed integer conversion
findings.description: Converting an unsigned integer to a signed type can produce a negative value if the unsigned value exceeds the signed type's maximum (e.g., uint256 > type(int256).max). In Solidity 0.8+, this reverts; in earlier versions, it wraps.
findings.recommendation: Validate that the value fits in the target signed type before casting. Use SafeCast for safe conversions.
